coverage_claim: WM-ACT-049 covers a source-qualified care-context aggregate that composes but does not collapse a CarePlan planning record and an EpisodeOfCare responsibility-tracking record. Goals, team participation, planned requests, tasks, encounters, performed activities, observations and transitions retain independent identities, states and times. Specialty profiles, jurisdiction rules, all three candidate registry relations, release-pinned mapping tests and independent external review remain deferred.

boundary_decision.rationale: The slash-labelled registry subject spans two separately identifiable but operationally related records: a care plan for intention and coordination and an episode for provider responsibility over time. Aggregate is more accurate than event or entity, while each constituent retains its own identity and lifecycle. The frozen record_plane world-model and catalogue entry_kind standalone-mm are separate axes from this subject-schema decision.

decisions.rationale: FHIR defines planning and provider responsibility tracking as distinct resources and explicitly distinguishes both from Encounter activity. The aggregate composes them without flattening status, time or authority.

decisions.concept: Goal, concern, observation and outcome separation
decisions.rationale: Goals describe desired states, conditions describe concerns and observations provide evaluation evidence. Achievement and outcome remain attributable assertions rather than consequences inferred from plan completion.

decisions.concept: Care team, plan authorship and episode responsibility
decisions.rationale: Care-team participation, plan authorship or custody, care management and managing-organization responsibility are different role bindings with their own scope and effective periods.
A plan may group intended request references and coordination constraints, but authorization, task execution, encounters and performed clinical events remain external masters with independent state.

PlanDefinition, RequestOrchestration and openEHR materials support versioned protocol links and action dependencies, but executable orchestration, clinical decision support and institutional workflow remain external and profile-specific.

WHO, NICE and IHE sources support person-centred participation, informational continuity, responsibility transfer, pending-work communication and acknowledgement without creating a universal clinical policy.

decisions.concept: Candidate WM-LIV-021, WM-ACT-047 and WM-ACT-048 relations
decisions.rationale: The relation ledger marks all three edges candidate. The specification may carry typed references but may not publish containment, lifecycle ownership or cascade behavior as approved.

decisions.concept: Standards maturity and retired workflow source
decisions.rationale: Most FHIR R5 planning resources are Trial Use at varied maturity, IHE DCP is an implementation profile and openEHR Task Planning Release-1.7.0 is retired. Every projection must pin version, status and information loss.

One Claude Sonnet and one Grok 4.6 research attempt each timed out after 120 seconds. Codex audited the frozen validated result and comparison locally without tools or new research facts. Confidence remains medium and assurance remains reviewable-draft.

publication_holds: Absence-of-external-review hold: one Claude Sonnet and one Grok 4.6 research attempt for WM-ACT-049 each timed out after 120 seconds. No external research result was admitted.
Registry edge approval hold: WM-ACT-049 REFERENCE WM-LIV-021 and CONTAINS WM-ACT-047 and WM-ACT-048 remain candidate metadata and create no cascade semantics.
Clinical-profile hold: oncology, mental health, maternity, pediatric, geriatric, rehabilitation, palliative, public-health, social-care, veterinary and research planning need specialty rules.

Jurisdiction and institution hold: capacity, guardianship, consent, care authority, scope of practice, assignment, transfer, escalation, reporting, retention and disclosure require applicable profiles.

Interoperability hold: FHIR maturity varies, IHE DCP is an implementation profile and openEHR Task Planning is retired; all mappings require release-pinned tests, loss declarations and clinical validation.
Aggregate-boundary hold: adopters must preserve independent plan and episode identities and may not treat the slash-labelled catalogue name as one undifferentiated lifecycle.
deferred_research: Approve or reject the three candidate relation-ledger edges and define cardinality, membership, ownership and non-cascade semantics.
Create specialty profiles for oncology, mental health, maternity, pediatric, geriatric, rehabilitation, palliative, public-health, social-care, veterinary and research care contexts.
Create jurisdiction and institution profiles for capacity, consent, care authority, roles, assignment, transfer, escalation, correction, retention and access.
Test release-pinned FHIR, IHE DCP and any successor workflow mappings with round-trip, maturity and information-loss evidence.
Obtain supplemental independent external review and resolve any material challenge before canonical promotion.
